packageRules.description: Crates: Cargo.lock within the caret ranges, or a range in Cargo.toml when a release falls outside it, both cargo roots, one pull request, with major updates in a pull request of their own beside it (separateMajorMinor). Held for dashboard approval while :dependencyDashboardApproval is in extends; a vulnerability-fix pull request skips that approval.

The upstream parser is never updated here. An upstream bump is a release of this repository (decisions 0010 and 0011), done through docs/how-to/bump-upstream.md, and just version-check fails a bare bump by design. The rule matches the manager rather than a file, so it covers both cargo roots; an exact requirement holds lock-file maintenance at the pin. This rule stays off for a vulnerability-fix pull request too: those rules never set enabled.

Remote actions, SHA and version comment together, one pull request, with major updates in a pull request of their own beside it (separateMajorMinor). Held for dashboard approval while :dependencyDashboardApproval is in extends; a vulnerability-fix pull request skips that approval.

The toolchain: channel in rust-toolchain.toml and rust-version in both manifests, one pull request. rust-release-channel versioning keeps the precision of the value it replaces, so rust-version stays major.minor. Held for dashboard approval, because a toolchain moves the clippy lint set; a vulnerability-fix pull request skips that approval.

Tool pins in pyproject.toml. Whether the hosted app relocks pixi.lock on this repository is read from the first approved branch; a stale pixi.lock fails lock-check. Held for dashboard approval; a vulnerability-fix pull request skips that approval.
python = "3.14.*" is the tooling interpreter (CONVENTIONS.md section 2), moved by hand, not a pin to bump; the manager would otherwise offer 3.15.*.
python-version inputs of setup-python are manual: 3.11 is the abi3 floor of decision 0012 and 3.14t is the free-threaded build the release matrix smokes, so neither is a version to bump.

The github-actions manager would read setup-uv's version and maturin-action's maturin-version from GitHub releases and PyPI, which can run ahead of conda-forge and split each from its pixi pin; the regex managers read them from conda-forge instead.
uv: the pin in pyproject.toml and the release job's setup-uv version, both read from conda-forge, one pull request. Held for dashboard approval; a vulnerability-fix pull request skips that approval.

maturin: the pin in pyproject.toml and every maturin-version input in the release workflow, both read from conda-forge, one pull request. Held for dashboard approval; a vulnerability-fix pull request skips that approval.

nextest-version in .config/nextest.toml equals the cargo-nextest pin in pyproject.toml, so both read conda-forge and move in one pull request. Held for dashboard approval; a vulnerability-fix pull request skips that approval.

The maturin range in build-system.requires. The pixi pin is what builds locally and in just check, and the release workflow sets maturin-version, so neither reads this range; it is what a user's installer honours when it builds the sdist. PyPI itself builds nothing. The range is kept rather than pinned, and Renovate proposes widening or replacing it on a maturin 2.0. Held for dashboard approval; a vulnerability-fix pull request skips that approval.
The tooling package's release tag: the checkers and the gate runner. Held for dashboard approval; a vulnerability-fix pull request skips that approval.
pixi itself: the requires-pixi floor in pyproject.toml and pixi-version in the setup action, one pull request. Held for dashboard approval; a vulnerability-fix pull request skips that approval.
The github-actions manager would read setup-pixi's pixi-version input under prefix-dev/pixi as well; the regex manager owns it.
Lock-file maintenance rewrites pixi.lock as well as both Cargo lockfiles. Held for dashboard approval; a vulnerability-fix pull request skips that approval.

Binaries in tools.txt and source builds in tools-source.txt. Each is a download nothing verifies beyond the transport or the registry checksum, and rustqual is a gate. Held for dashboard approval; a vulnerability-fix pull request skips that approval.

twine in the release workflow's check of every job's dist/: first exercised by the release rehearsal, because the workflow does not run on pull requests. Held for dashboard approval; a vulnerability-fix pull request skips that approval.
Hook revs in both prek configs, one pull request, because a hook is code the gate runs on every commit. Held for dashboard approval; a vulnerability-fix pull request skips that approval.
lychee moves by hand: LYCHEE_VERSION in both argument lists must match its rev, and its tag prefix is lychee-v.

customManagers.description: rust-version in the workspace and fuzz manifests, grouped with the native rust-toolchain manager's channel.
tools.txt and tools-source.txt: one name@version per line, resolved on crates.io.
nextest-version, which must equal the cargo-nextest pin in pyproject.toml, read from the same conda-forge package.

The release job's setup-uv version, which must equal the uv pin in pyproject.toml, read from the same conda-forge package. The pattern is bound to the setup-uv step, so another action's version input is not read; version must stay the step's first input, or this stops matching.
maturin-action's maturin-version inputs, which must equal the maturin pin in pyproject.toml, read from the same conda-forge package.
twine in the release workflow's TWINE_CHECK script.
requires-pixi, the floor that moves with pixi-version in the setup action.
setup-pixi's pixi-version input, read here rather than by the github-actions manager, under the requires-pixi floor's depName.
Hook revs in both prek configs: a full SHA with the release tag as its comment. lychee's lychee-v comment does not match.
